followUpGuide: For glob matching, compile patterns once and preserve rule order.
For repeated filtering, parse each rule into `{negated, prefix, pattern}` before scanning paths.
This filter controls which paths enter indexing or upload. A re-include rule can restore a path, so enforce authorization independently for file reads, tools, uploads, and retrieval.
complexityAnalysis: - Let p be candidate count, r be rule count, and L bound path/rule length. Parsing and validation cost O((p+r)*L); ordered matching costs O(p*r*L). Total time is O((p+r+p*r)*L), including empty-input cases.

- The shown solution already compiles rules once. Auxiliary space is O(r*L+L) for retained rule strings and temporary path segments, plus O(p) references in the output. Reusing compiled rules across calls avoids repeating parsing.
- Glob follow-up can raise match cost, so the production path should precompile patterns.
solutionGuide: Strip each rule, parse its optional negation and directory suffix, then validate the remaining pattern. Validate candidate paths without normalizing them. Track whether each candidate is ignored as you scan rules in order; the last matching rule wins.
